verdict_reason: TranscriptAPI documents a public REST API at https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2 with 13 GET endpoints spanning transcripts, video metadata, search, channels, and playlists, plus a hosted MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp. The docs show a free self-serve signup and a dashboard API key used as a Bearer token, with a one-request cURL/Python quick start and no sales contact or app review described. The absence of official SDKs, a sandbox, and documented rate-limit numbers does not block raw REST integration.
open_questions: App-name ambiguity: the input app is 'YouTube Transcript' but the researched product is TranscriptAPI (transcriptapi.com). Disambiguated via the Composio catalog slug youtube_transcript and the vendor's own page titles; confirm this is not meant to be the open-source 'youtube-transcript-api' library.
The pricing page (https://transcriptapi.com/pricing) returned only image markup in the fetched text, so the exact free-tier credit allotment and paid plan prices could not be verified from page text.
No OAuth scope/permission definitions were found; OAuth 2.1 appears documented only for the hosted MCP server via dynamic or static client registration.
Rate-limit numbers and per-plan quotas were not present in the fetched sources; a JavaScript getting-started page (not included in this bundle) reportedly mentions HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header.
No webhook/event callback documentation was found; the vendor's channel-monitoring guide appears to check for new uploads on a schedule (polling) rather than via events.
No sandbox or test environment is documented beyond an interactive Swagger UI for live requests.
No official vendor-maintained SDKs were found; the vendor comparison article implies only Supadata publishes Python/JS SDKs.
No community MCP servers were identified (GitHub and MCP registry checks returned no results in this bundle).
